headline: Princeton researcher's ICE detention rattles academia
pages: Eva Yi Xie, a Princeton graduate student and researcher, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Thursday while traveling home from the Society for Neuroscience conference in Washington. She has lived in the US since 2016 after moving from China. Her visa had expired, according to The New York Times, but her lawyers say a pending asylum application allows her to remain legally. ICE did not say why she was held. The news spread quickly Friday because it highlighted fears among foreign-born academics and students that traveling to present research is too risky.

Johns Hopkins academic Caitlin Rivers said it is an open question whether it is safe for people on student visas to travel, noting a staff member of hers was detained earlier this year. Some US conferences have reported smaller attendance in the past two years. The White House has said it wants fewer foreign-born graduate students. Source: STAT News.
